subject: EU-only processing, backups & SCCs — PolarisHealth follow-up
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@polarishealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: PolarisHealth Security <security@polarishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jan 2028 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: EU processing / SCCs questions for evaluation

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — PolarisHealth is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we move forward with a pilot, our InfoSec team has a few gating questions around EU-only processing and SCCs:

- Can you confirm whether production customer data can be guaranteed to stay within the EU (processing AND backups)?
- What is Redwood's operating model for backups and disaster recovery blobs that may be stored outside the serving region?
- Have you executed the EU standard contractual clauses (SCCs) with Redwood as a data exporter/processor? If so, can we get a redacted copy and evidence of signing?
- Which sub-processors may access logs or debug traces and do any of them reside outside the EEA?

I've attached our security questionnaire (CSV) — the team flagged these items as blockers for our legal review. We'd prefer a short written response and (if possible) a one-hour technical call next week to walk through the architecture.

Thanks,
Daniel Park\Security & Compliance Lead\PolarisHealth
Attachments: Polaris_Security_Questionnaire.csv
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@polarishealth.com>
Cc: PolarisHealth Security <security@polarishealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jan 2028 11:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU processing / SCCs questions for evaluation

Hi Daniel — thanks for sending this over and for the great session. I pulled together concise answers below and attached a short plan that maps our controls to your questionnaire references. Happy to join a technical call; how does Thursday 12:00 CET look?

Quick answers (high level):
- EU-only processing: Yes — for hosted and private deployments we support region-pinning at the request/tenant level. For PolarisHealth pilot we can configure all processing and persistent storage (including snapshot/backups) to remain in the selected EU region(s).
- Backups/DR: By default snapshots are stored in the same cloud region. We do offer an optional cross-region replication policy for customer-configured DR — that would be an explicit opt-in and documented in the mutual action plan.
- SCCs: Redwood maintains executed SCCs for our hosted customers; we can provide a redacted executed copy and a signing manifest. For Dedicated/Private contracts we sign either SCCs or equivalent contractual addenda depending on legal preference.
- Sub-processors and logs: We maintain a current sub-processor list; role-based access to logs is limited to named infra/support engineers and our cloud provider contractors. For an EU-only tenancy we can ensure the sub-processors who access logs are EU-resident or operate under subcontractor agreements that restrict cross-border access.

Next steps I propose (short):
1) I will loop in Laura and Neha to prepare: (a) redacted SCCs + signing manifest, (b) a short architecture diagram showing backups/replication controls, (c) sub-processor roster with residency info.
2) Technical call Thursday 12:00 CET — I can host. Please confirm attendee list.

Attaching: SCCs_execution_plan_v1.pdf, redwood-eu-data-flow-20280111.png

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni\Head of Solutions Engineering\Redwood Inference
Attachments: SCCs_execution_plan_v1.pdf, redwood-eu-data-flow-20280111.png
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Jan 2028 08:35:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: PolarisHealth - prepare SCCs/redaction and sub-processor table (internal)

Laura / Neha — quick internal note and ask ahead of Thursday's call. Daniel at PolarisHealth pushed the questionnaire; they want three deliverables by EOW: redacted executed SCCs, confirmation that backups will remain in EU for the pilot, and a list of sub-processors with locations.

Can you please: 
- Laura: pull the executed SCCs bundle for hosted customers (redact signatures/PII) and generate a one-paragraph signing manifest (who signed, date, jurisdiction).
- Neha: produce a two-column sub-processor table (component | location | reason for access) and confirm whether any support/debug traces are routed to non-EEA engineers for incident response.

Notes / constraints:
- For backups: the default config keeps snapshots in-region. If legal insists on strict in-region-for-all-time we should flag the optional cross-region DR is an opt-in and we can provide an SLA attachment.
- If Polaris requires that no non-EEA sub-processors ever access logs, we should be explicit about replacement timelines and whether Dedicated/Private is required.

I'll take the architecture diagram and the customer-facing summary. I will also prep a short answer set to the specific CSV rows Daniel flagged.

Thanks — Vivek
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@polarishealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: PolarisHealth Security <security@polarishealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jan 2028 15:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU processing / SCCs questions for evaluation

Vivek — appreciate the quick summary and the attachments. Thursday worked well; the security team is satisfied with the in-region defaults and the option model for DR as long as cross-region replication is explicitly documented and opt-in.

Two asks to close the gating review: 
1) Signed/redacted SCCs and the signing manifest (we need to show legal the signature trail).
2) A clear statement in writing that for the PolarisHealth pilot all backups and diagnostic logs will be stored and retained in the EU and will not be replicated outside the EEA unless Polaris explicitly opts into DR replication.

If you can send both items and a DocuSign-ready SCCs packet we will route for signature next week. Assuming those are in place we can move forward with the pilot PO.

Thanks,
Daniel
Security & Compliance Lead\PolarisHealth
Attachments referenced: none
